report_name: Web3 Casino Intraverse.io Leaks 16.9M Records From Unsecured Database

threat_actors.name: exfilar
threat_actors.description: The threat actor who discovered and published the unsecured Intraverse.io Firebase database on a hacking forum. The actor used bulk scanning techniques to find the misconfigured cloud resource.

attack_patterns.name: Search Open Technical Databases
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used a bulk scan of Firebase project identifiers (e.g., `[project-id].firebaseio.com/.json`) to find the open database instance, which is a form of searching open technical databases for misconfigured resources.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The attacker exfiltrated the entire contents of the misconfigured Firebase Realtime Database by making an HTTP GET request to the database's root URL with '.json' appended.

vulnerabilities.name: Firebase Publicly Readable Database Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.description: The Intraverse.io Firebase Realtime Database had its security rules misconfigured to be publicly readable (e.g., `{".read": "true"}`), allowing unauthenticated access to the entire database.

identities.name: Intraverse.io
identities.description: A Web3 online gambling platform that suffered a major data breach due to a misconfigured Firebase Realtime Database, exposing approximately 16.9 million records.

infrastructure.name: Hacking Forum
infrastructure.description: A hacking forum where the threat actor 'exfilar' published the leaked database from Intraverse.io.

indicators.name: Publicly Accessible Firebase Database Discovery Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Publicly Accessible Firebase Database Discovery Attempt
id: 2b1a9c8d-5f6e-4b3a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to discover publicly accessible Firebase databases by appending '/.json' to the domain, a common scanning technique.
references:
  - https://darkwebinformer.com/web3-casino-intraverse-allegedly-exposed-by-a-keyless-firebase-database-including-its-own-house-bot-stack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1596
  - attack.t1595
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|endswith: '.firebaseio.com/.json'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network requests attempting to discover publicly accessible Firebase databases by appending `/.json` to the domain, as described in the Intraverse.io breach report.
